provenance.description: Phase-only advisory scheduling hypothesis with all 540 source hashes preserved. Latest successful measured nodes replace earlier observations; failed newer nodes retain their previous successful observation. First three shared-fixture groups retain consumer call/teardown plus one maximum observed cold setup. Fourth serial group retains both independent setup/call/teardown costs. No native quality-bound speed scaling is applied.
prediction_limitations: Advisory timing hypotheses, not acceptance evidence; failed newer nodes retain prior actual successful costs.
Costs are actual setup/call/teardown phases only; no quality-bound or native-microbench saving is applied.
Current observations use Linux four, Mac three and Windows two local workers; Windows three/four-worker predictions reuse those costs without assuming a speed gain.
Quality-tool concurrency, runtime-prefix contents, host speed and assignment co-location confound comparisons.
Conservative overhead adds separate observed parent/join and worker maxima; it excludes launch skew and does not bound future host variation.
Original tests, real installs, fresh fingerprints, finite deadlines and exact node/phase/coverage gates remain required.
